original_question: In the inductive growth description of CTCS(n), let p_up be the limiting probability of branch extension and let p_diag be the limiting probability of side-bud extension. Because the analysis suggests p_up = p_diag, determine whether this identity is a consequence of an underlying symmetry of the random tree shape.
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Open Problem 9, together with the immediately stated equivalent reformulation that the limiting branch-extension and side-bud-extension probabilities should coincide and might reflect a hidden symmetry of the tree shape.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right model (CTCS(n)), the right local mechanism (the inductive growth construction), the two relevant growth types (branch extension and side-bud extension), and the paper's qualitative motivation that any equality between their limiting probabilities should come from an underlying symmetry of the random tree shape.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation in the paper is not stated first as p_up = p_diag, but as an equality between the linear tree-length constant from equation (60) and a(2); the paper then says this is equivalent to equality of the two growth-type probabilities.

The draft omits the quantifier/assumption that these are only expected limiting probabilities as n -> infinity; in Section 7.1 the paper says it expects that such limits exist, rather than taking their existence as already proved.
The third growth type, side-bud addition, and its limiting probability p→ are omitted, although the paper explicitly lists all three placement types in the inductive construction.
The paper's notation for the two probabilities is p↑ and p↗, not p_up and p_diag.

The paper uses slightly inconsistent terminology: in Section 3 case (c) is the event where a side-bud grows into a new branch with two terminal buds, called there a side-leaf extension, while Section 7.1 refers to its limiting probability as the side-bud extension probability.
The meaning of a(2) is missing: a(2) = lim_{n->infinity} a(n,2), where a(n,i) is the probability that the size-biased clade-size chain started at state n ever visits state i.
The draft does not mention the exact equivalence used in Section 7.1: the length constant equals p↑ + p↗, while a(2) = 2p↗, so equality of the two constants is equivalent to p↑ = p↗.
The draft omits the paper's first interpretation of the same equality: asymptotically, exactly half of the total tree length lies in the terminal edges leading to bud-pairs.
refined_question: In the canonical inductive construction of the continuous-time critical splitting tree CTCS(n+1) from CTCS(n), suppose that as n -> infinity the probabilities of the three possible placements of the new bud converge to limits p↑, p→, and p↗, corresponding respectively to branch extension, side-bud addition, and the case in which a side-bud grows into a new branch with two terminal buds. Must p↑ = p↗, and if so can this equality be explained by a hidden symmetry of the limiting random tree shape?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is the linear tree-length constant in equation (60) equal to a(2), where a(2) = lim_{n->infinity} a(n,2) and a(n,2) is the probability that the size-biased clade-size chain started at n ever visits state 2?
justification: The draft is aimed at the second, shape-theoretic interpretation given in Section 7.1 rather than at the displayed equation of Open Problem 9 itself. The nearby context shows that the paper first asks whether the linear tree-length constant equals a(2), and then immediately states that this is equivalent to p↑ = p↗; it adds that this latter form is more naturally interpretable as a symmetry of tree shape. To make the question stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import from Section 3 the three growth mechanisms in the inductive construction and from Proposition 12 the definition of a(2) via the occupation measure of the size-biased chain.
